newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close 2.04 pct lower on economy.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close 2.04 pct lower on economy.

text.p: Concerns over the country's economy along with a negative creditwatch on Thailand by Standard & Poor's Corp prompted investors to sell and drove the index to close 2.04 percent lower on Friday, brokers said.
The composite SET index closed 13.58 points lower at 652.04 on 3.5 billion baht turnover.

"Poor market sentiment continued from yesterday. Investors thought the outlook of the country's economy was poor. Their main concern is foreign reserves," said Busaba Kunasirin of Chao Phya Finance and Securities.
Foreign reserves figures, released by the Bank of Thailand on Thursday, showed that they stood at $32.4 billion in June, a drop from $33.3 billion in May.
Brokers said July figures might be more telling as the bank was forced to defend the currency after floating the baht in early July.
"Reports earlier today on S&P on placing negative creditwatch on Thailand also affected the market," Busaba said.
S&P said it had placed a negative creditwatch on Thai foreign currency and eight financial institutions, including the country's largest bank, Bangkok Bank Plc.
The ratings agency said its action reflected concerns that non-performing loans and loan losses would rise to levels not consistent with current ratings.
Brokers said investors were a bit surprised that the agency had placed the negative creditwatch on Bangkok Bank.
These worries led investors to unload finance, communication and bank stocks, which dropped 6.08, 2.64 and 1.66 percent respectively.

Eastern Water Resources Development and Management Plc topped the active list in terms of value, gaining 4.25 baht to 48.75. Nava Finance lost three to 30.25 while Thai Farmers Bank shed one to 115 and Advance Info retreated 12 to 216.
